象牙號起源於非洲和中東地區，古代人類利用大象或其他大型動物的象牙製作。這種樂器最: The olifant originated in Africa and the Middle East, where people in ancient times made it from the ivory of elephants and other large animals. The instrument first appears in the civilisations of Egypt and Mesopotamia, used for hunting signals and religious ritual. In the Middle Ages the olifant reached Europe and was widely used in particular in the Frankish empire, becoming a symbol of noble status and power. According to medieval epics such as the Song of Roland, the olifant played an important part in military campaigns, carrying orders across the battlefield. Over time its making was refined and its decoration grew more elaborate, often carved with intricate patterns and inscriptions. By the Renaissance the olifant was not only an instrument but a work of decorative art. Its distinctive, deep timbre and great volume made it highly prized in medieval knightly culture and at court.
